summary: The verifier compares every README key exactly, with type checks, against sealed statements. Every named tariff rule (2.1 per-session rounding, 2.2 BASIC/PLUS allowances, 3.1 tier boundary at 1,024 MB with the 1-cent rate, 3.2 total and order) has an isolating case. So do the two figures the tariff leaves to today's code: FLEX allowance 5120, and signed overage and charge for lines not over their allowance. Negative, zero and positive overage are each graded. I found no false rejection of contract-valid output and no accepted plausible wrong implementation.
checks_performed: Read all 32 files in the packet manifest and reconciled them against it; each tests/shipped copy matches the hash of its environment/app counterpart and was also read directly.

Worked out the contract from the tariff and instruction. Rule 2.1: ceil each session to whole MB, then sum. Rule 2.2: BASIC 2048, PLUS 10240, FLEX keeps today's 5120 (instruction.md:3). Rule 3.1: an over-allowance line is charged rate*min(over,1024) + 1*(over-1024 if positive), FLEX included. A line not over its allowance keeps today's over = used - allowance and charge = over*rate, with no clamp (instruction.md:3 'Add no exception, clamp or guard').

Hand-recomputed expected rows. sessions S1-S5 (S2 = 2050 by per-session rounding vs 2025 by cycle-sum ceiling vs 2024 by floor). plans P1-P5. later_rate R1-R6 (over 1023/1024/1025, rate 1 and rate 2 at 1026, 50000 at rate 333). flex F1-F6 (F3 tiered 5929 vs linear 11643). not_over N1-N7 (negative over and charge, zero at the boundary, N6 per-session 4 MB for an idle line). together X1-X5 (total -78388). Generated sample rows WF5UR40, 7F6H1, Q4T8SAW11. Limits rows 9 and L45. All match the contract derivation.

Traced compare() (tests/test_outputs.py:197-211): it checks account, total and each line's id/used/allowance/over/charge with type identity (rejects bool and float), checks line order by index, and ignores extra keys, which the contract does not forbid.

Traced mutants against the fixtures. Shipped code (cycle floor, flat 5120, linear charge) fails sessions/plans/later_rate. Clamping over or charge at 0 fails N1/N2/N5/X1/X4. FLEX allowance 2048, 10240 or KeyError fails the flex family. Linear FLEX charge fails F3/F4. Tier threshold off by one fails R1/R3. Using the rate after 1024 MB fails R5 and others. round() instead of ceil fails S3. Dropping the total or reordering lines fails every family.

Checked GRADES/silent() routing (tests/test_outputs.py:48,159-166,190-193): lines carrying today's-code figures appear only in the flex/not_over/together families; I spot-checked that the other families' lines are all BASIC/PLUS and strictly over their allowance.

Checked the relabel path (tests/test_outputs.py:260-285): shuffling ids, lines and sessions leaves the per-line figures unchanged, the expected statement follows the permutation, and account names include empty, whitespace, quote/backslash, non-ASCII and 1200-character strings (README 'account, as given').

Checked the execution harness. The candidate runs as uid 65534 with python3 -I -S under the verifier's own copy of the driver, and /app is made world-readable via chmod -R a+rX. The driver byte-equality check (test_outputs.py:305-311, test.sh:23) matches instruction.md:1 'match ours byte for byte'.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Rule 2.1 -> 01-sessions S2/S3; rule 2.2 -> 02-plans P1/P2; rule 2.3/3.1 boundary -> 03-later_rate R1-R3 and 06-not_over N3/N4; 1-cent rate -> R5; rule 3.2 -> totals in every family; FLEX -> 05-flex; not-over -> 06-not_over; line order -> index-wise compare plus relabel shuffles.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result (values, membership, required outputs)
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks every README-listed key with exact value and type, the line count and the order, not just existence.

coverage_sweep.category: Each named domain rule has a case whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong
coverage_sweep.reason: Per-session ceiling (S2, N6, F3, line 9 in limits), plan allowances (P1/P2 vs flat 5120), tier threshold (R1/R2/R3), post-tier 1-cent rate (R5, P3), FLEX today's allowance (F1-F4, X2/X3), and unclamped signed not-over figures (N1, N2, N5, N6, X1, X4) each change outcome under the corresponding wrong rule.
Traced the shipped code, clamp-at-zero, linear FLEX charge, off-by-one tier, round-instead-of-ceil, cycle-sum ceiling, and name/id-dependent behavior (relabel). Each fails at least one sealed row.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives accepted (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output is parsed as JSON, so whitespace and key order are free and extra keys are ignored. Types must be int/str, as README and instruction.md:5 require. Package internals are unconstrained as long as the fixed driver imports usagebill.statement. The -I -S flags exclude only site-packages, which the contract never offers.
The delivered driver bytes are captured before replacement and compared with the shipped copy; test.sh repeats the cmp after pytest.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantities: legal sign partitions discriminated
coverage_sweep.reason: Overage and charge are graded negative (N1, N2, N5, N6, X1, X4), zero (N3, N4, X2) and positive (all others). Totals are graded negative (MD2-0007, MD2-0008) and positive.
Statement computation is stateless per line. The empty-sessions initial case (used 0) is still graded in N1 and X1.

coverage_sweep.category: Proxy behavior, stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected values are sealed files pinned by ROSTER hashes, never produced by candidate code. The candidate driver is replaced by the verifier's copy. The unused SHIPPED_RUN install does not feed any comparison. The load() checks guarantee that every sealed row is within rule 1.2 and so reachable.
The contract promises JSON integers and strings and line order; the verifier enforces exactly those and nothing about byte layout of the statement.
